transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, it’s the people in my apartment building. They’re watching when I come in and out, I know they are, and they’re slipping notes about me to the office. Everybody keeps saying, “No, those are just notices on the doors,” but that’s not what it feels like. I see how it all lines up.

I mean, I’ve lived in apartments before, and there’s always someone keeping track of things—maintenance, managers, neighbors with too much time. But this is different. It’s like my comings and goings are being reported, and nobody wants to admit it.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people can't hear?

I don’t know… I mean, people say things in the hallway sometimes, and the walls are thin, so it’s hard to tell what’s meant for me or what’s just somebody talking. I haven’t really sat there thinking, “that’s a voice nobody else can hear,” if that’s what you mean.

But in that building, sounds carry funny. Pipes, doors, people upstairs dragging chairs—at night it all blends together. So… I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say I hear voices like that, no.
Do you find it hard to keep track of your thoughts or make sense of what's happening around you?

Yeah… I mean, sometimes when I try to explain it, it comes out wrong. Like I’ll start talking about the rent, because that’s where it started, or I think it did, and then I’m thinking about the marina—there was a thing there before, not exactly the same, but connected—and then I’m telling somebody about the choir robes, and the wires in the walls, and they look at me like I skipped half the story.

But in my head it makes sense. It’s just when I say it out loud, people act like I jumped from one thing to another.
Do you often find yourself switching between different ideas or topics when thinking or talking?

Yeah… I guess I do. Not on purpose. Like I’ll be trying to explain one thing, the rent maybe, because that’s where it starts, or where I think it starts, and then I’m talking about the marina, and then the choir robes come into it, and the wires in the walls, and people get that look like I left out a whole chunk.

But to me it’s connected. It just doesn’t come out in the right order, I suppose.
Do you feel like your thoughts are racing or speeding up when you're trying to explain something?

Not racing exactly… it’s more like I can’t keep it lined up. I’ll start trying to explain the rent, because that’s the part people understand, and then the marina comes in—because that was connected somehow—and then I’m thinking about the choir robes, and the wires in the walls, and before I know it people are staring at me like I skipped half the story.

So maybe it sounds fast to them, I don’t know. In my head I’m just trying to get to the part that matters.
Do you have difficulty completing tasks or following through with plans due to your thoughts or feelings?

Yeah… I do. I mean, I try to make a plan, like pay the bills or get to an appointment, and then the day gets away from me. Or I start thinking about whether I should even go, whether the person at the desk is going to act strange, and then I don’t go.

I’ve fallen behind on bills that way. Missed appointments. And church too… I used to show up more, and there were volunteer things I said I’d help with, but I just stopped going. Not because I don’t care. I just can’t keep the days straight, and regular conversations start feeling like too much to trust.
Do you have difficulty taking care of your personal appearance or daily needs?

Yeah… some days it’s hard. I’ll be sitting there knowing I need to get dressed, just put on a shirt and shoes, and it takes me forever. Even walking out to the mailbox, I feel so slow, like if the old neighbors saw me they’d think, “That’s not him.”

Then other days I’m the opposite. I’m up pacing around my little apartment, checking the window, then checking it again, and I forget I was supposed to wash up or change clothes. It’s not that I don’t want to look decent. I just… I don’t always get myself moving right.
Do you often find yourself doing things that don't make sense to others or seem unusual?

Yeah… I guess so. Like at the senior-center workshop, they had us fixing a shelf, and I was supposed to be helping, but I got stuck lining up the screws by size. Little ones, then the longer ones, and I kept tapping the table, like that was part of it.

And I know the shelf was the point, but my hands just kept doing that. The lady asked me to sit down, and I was just standing there holding the screwdriver. Like I couldn’t change over to what she was saying. I could tell it looked odd.
Do you feel like your thoughts are getting jumbled or mixed up when you're trying to think clearly?

Yeah… they do get mixed up. I’ll be trying to explain one thing, like the rent, and then I’m talking about the marina, and then somehow I’m on choir robes from church, and the wires in the walls… and I can see people looking at me like I left out the middle part.

In my head it feels connected when I start, but when it comes out, it’s like I skipped steps. Then I get embarrassed and try to fix it, but that sometimes makes it worse.
Do you often find yourself engaging in behaviors that seem pointless or without a clear goal?

Yeah… I think so. Like I said about that workshop at the senior center, I was supposed to be helping fix the shelf, but I got all caught up putting the screws in order by size. Then I was tapping the table with them, just… doing that instead of actually working on the shelf.

And the lady told me to sit down, but I just stood there holding the screwdriver. It was like my body didn’t catch up with what she said, or I couldn’t switch over. It probably looked pointless, yeah.
Do you often have trouble expressing your thoughts in a way that makes sense to others?

Yeah… I do. I’ll start trying to explain something simple, like the rent, and then I’m talking about the marina for some reason, and then choir robes at church, and then wires in the walls… and people look at me like I skipped half the story.

It makes sense in my head at first, like there’s a path there, but when I say it out loud it comes out all sideways. Then I can tell I lost them.
Do you believe that the people in your apartment building are actually watching you and reporting on your activities?

Yes… that’s why I came in, really. The people in my building, they watch when I leave and when I come back. I can tell by the way the hallway goes quiet, and then there’ll be papers on the doors, and everybody says, “Those are just notices,” but no… some of it is about me. They’re slipping notes to the office about what I’m doing.

And the office acts like they don’t know, but they know. It’s like when the mail gets put in the wrong slot, and then you have to go downstairs, and the woman with the little dog is always there right when you— I’m sorry. But yes, I do believe they’re reporting on me.
Do you often feel like your thoughts are disconnected from each other?

Yeah… disconnected, that’s a good word for it. I’ll be trying to explain one thing, like the rent, and then somehow I’m talking about the marina, and then the choir robes at church, and then the wires in the walls.

In my head it feels like there’s a reason I got from one to the other, but people look at me like I skipped half the story. Like I left out the part that connects it, but I don’t always know what part that was.
Have you believed that people in your apartment building are watching you for a long time, or is this a relatively new feeling?

It’s… not brand new. I mean, I’ve been feeling that way for about a year and a month, maybe around there.

At first I thought it was just neighbors being nosy, because apartments are like that, you hear doors and footsteps and the office puts papers up, and there’s always somebody by the mailboxes… but it kept feeling like it was about me. So, yeah, it’s been over a year.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your daily life or behavior over the past year?

Yeah… I mean, yes. Things have kind of fallen apart in regular ways, not like one big thing, but the small things that keep piling up.

I get behind on bills because I’ll put them somewhere safe, and then I don’t know if I should call the office or if they’re going to twist it around, and then the envelope sits there. I’ve missed appointments too. I write them down, but then the day gets mixed up, or I start thinking I shouldn’t go because of who might be there.

And church… I used to go more. I had things I was supposed to help with, and some volunteer stuff too, but I just stopped showing up. It’s hard to keep the days straight, and it’s hard to know when a normal conversation is just normal, you know? So I stay back, and then people get upset because I didn’t come.
Have you ever thought that the people watching you were part of a larger conspiracy?

I don’t know if I’d call it a whole conspiracy exactly… but it feels organized, yes. Like the people in my building are keeping track of when I leave and when I come back, and then little notes show up, or notices on doors, and everybody says, “No, that’s just from the office,” but it doesn’t feel like just that.

Because it’s always around the same times, you know? Like when I go downstairs or pass the mailboxes, and then someone is standing there pretending to sort coupons or something. My cousin used to save coupons in a shoebox, which was smart, really, because groceries are ridiculous now… but, sorry. What I mean is, it feels like they’re watching me and passing things along to the apartment office about me.
Do you often find it hard to stick to one topic when talking to someone?

Yeah… I guess I do. I don’t always notice it while I’m talking, but people will look at me like I left something out.

Like I’ll start trying to explain about the rent, and then I’m talking about the marina, because that connects in my head, and then somehow I’m on choir robes or the wires in the walls, and people act like I skipped half the story. But to me it felt like I was getting there, you know? It’s hard to keep it all in one straight line.
Do you still believe that the people in your apartment building are watching you and reporting on your activities?

Yes… I still believe it. I know people keep saying it’s just regular notices from the office, like maintenance or rent things, but it doesn’t feel regular to me.

They watch when I come and go. Like if I go downstairs, somebody’s there, and then later there’s a note on the door or something gets said through the office. It’s like they’re slipping information about me over there. I mean, I came in because of that, really… because everybody keeps telling me I’m reading it wrong, but I don’t think I am.
Have you ever considered the possibility that the people in your apartment building are not actually watching you?

I’ve tried to consider it because everybody keeps telling me that, you know, “It’s just notices on the doors,” or “That’s just the office doing their job.” But I came in because I don’t think it’s just that.

It’s the timing. People at my apartment know when I leave and when I come back, and then somehow notes show up or things get passed to the office about me. I know that probably sounds… I don’t know, like I’m making connections, but if you lived there and saw it every day, you’d see what I mean.

And the office acts like it’s nothing, like maintenance papers or rent reminders, but it feels like they’re slipping information about me over there. I’ve thought maybe I’m wrong, sure, but it doesn’t feel wrong.
Have you ever considered that your beliefs about being watched might not be true, and would you be willing to change your mind if presented with evidence to the contrary?

I mean… I’ve tried to think that, because everybody keeps saying maybe it’s just normal notices on the doors or the office doing what they do. But I came in because I know the people at my apartment are watching when I leave and come back.

It’s not just one thing. It’s like, I go out, somebody sees me, then later there’s a note, or the office knows something. And people say, “No, that’s just rent stuff,” but it doesn’t feel like that. It feels like they’re slipping notes about me over there.

So… evidence, I don’t know. I’d listen, I guess, but it would have to explain all of that, not just tell me I’m wrong.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with persistent delusional beliefs of being watched and monitored by people in their apartment building, which have been ongoing for over a year. These beliefs are not explainable by any other mental disorder and are not a result of substance use or a medical condition. The patient also exhibits disorganized thinking and speech, as evidenced by their difficulty in maintaining a coherent conversation and tendency to jump between topics. However, the presence of prominent delusions and the absence of prominent hallucinations, disorganized behavior, or negative symptoms suggest a diagnosis of Delusional Disorder.
